seoTitle: Sight Reading Trainer: Name the Note on the Staff
metaDescription: Notes appear on a treble or bass staff; name them with buttons or letter keys and get your speed and mistakes. Free, no sign-up.
intro: Shows random notes on a treble or bass staff for you to name, with an optional time limit and a summary of your speed and mistakes.
why:
Reading music quickly means knowing the lines and spaces without counting. A staff is drawn with one note at a time, and you answer with the letter, by button or by pressing A to G.

A round has 20 notes. The summary gives your score, your average answer time and the notes you missed. The picture has a text description and the buttons are real controls, so the trainer can be used with a keyboard. Range is from two ledger lines below the staff to one above it. Nothing is stored.
howTo: Choose the clef and a time limit.
Name each note with a button or key A to G.

faq.q: Does it use sharps and flats?
How does the time limit work?
faq.a: If you do not answer in time the note counts as missed.

faq.q: Is it for screen reader users?
faq.a: The staff has a text label but the exercise itself is visual.
The clef is named in text; the symbol is not drawn.
